ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the graph of the linear function $y=kx+b$ intersects with the graph of the inverse proportion function $y=\frac{4}{x}$ (where $x>0$) at points $A(m, 4)$ and $B(2, n)$, and intersects with the coordinate axes at points $M$ and $N$, respectively. What is the analytical expression of the linear function?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that A $(1, 4)$ and B $(2, 2)$ are on the graph of the inverse proportion function $y=\frac{4}{x}$,

\[
\therefore
\begin{cases}
4=\frac{4}{m} \\
n=\frac{4}{2}
\end{cases}
\text{, which implies }
\begin{cases}
m=1 \\
n=2
\end{cases},
\]
thus A $(1, 4)$ and B $(2, 2)$.

Substituting A $(1, 4)$ and B $(2, 2)$ into $y=kx+b$, we get:
\[
\begin{cases}
4=k+b \\
2=2k+b
\end{cases}
\]
which solves to:
\[
\begin{cases}
k=-2 \\
b=6
\end{cases},
\]
therefore, the equation of the linear function is \boxed{y=-2x+6}.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a plane rectangular coordinate system, with the x-axis pointing to the right and the y-axis pointing upward; in the first quadrant there is an inverse proportional function curve (one branch of a hyperbola), and there is also a straight line slanting downward to the right. The straight line and the curve have two common intersection points, the upper-left one is labeled A, and the lower-right one is labeled B; the straight line also intersects the y-axis and the x-axis respectively, and the intersection points are labeled M and N. The figure also draws auxiliary lines pointing from the origin O to A and B. From the figure it can be known that A and B are the intersection points of the straight line y=kx+b and the inverse proportional function y=4/x. Reasoning: The problem gives A(m,4), B(2,n), and both A and B are on the inverse proportional function y=4/x. Substitute A(m,4) into y=4/x to get 4=4/m, so m=1. Substitute B(2,n) into y=4/x to get n=4/2=2. Therefore A=(1,4), B=(2,2). Because A and B are also on the straight line y=kx+b, use two points to determine the straight line. The slope k=(2-4)/(2-1)=-2. Then substitute A(1,4) into y=-2x+b to get 4=-2·1+b, so b=6. Therefore the analytic expression of the straight line is y=-2x+6.
